Issue Number: close #35414

Problem Summary:
support encoding and decoding session variables. This is used for the session manager.

### What is changed and how it works?
Encode the states in `session.EncodeSessionStates()` and decodes them in `session.DecodeSessionStates()`.
Read-only variables are ignored in this PR. They will be handled in the next PR.
We don't need to document it because it won't be exposed to users.

issue_context.title: support encoding session variables for session manager
issue_context.body:
The session manager needs to get all the states for the current session through `show session_states` and restore them on the other session through `set session_states ...`.
This includes session variables.

review_comments: Can't we just return an error if `keep(bool) == false`?

It's weird, because it may not be an error when `keep==false`.
E.g. When `timestamp` is never set, we don't keep it, but it's not an error, it's normal.
Well, I think it is good to use `errors.Is` or so to judge errors. But if you like an additional variable...

> GetSession may not return the real value

Could you give an example that 'real value' is required for migration?

Examples are given in the test cases.
E.g. `select @@rand_seed1` always returns 0, but the real value is not 0.

Why not invoke `GetSessionFromHook` directly? It has a  guard on `sv.GetSession != nil `. The differences are only:

1. none scope check
2. relax validation
3. fallback to stmtvars also

When the variable is not in `systems`, `GetSessionFromHook()` throws an error.
But when `GetSessionFromHook()` throws an error, we don't know whether it should continue. It may be a marshal error from `GetSession()` (we should break), or a `sysvar has not yet loaded` error (we should continue). One way is to check the error message, which is ugly.
